absent: Numeric values and full enumerations for hide levels, ptrace modes, file flags, oom limits, clock identifiers, and error codes.
Field layouts and size or alignment for task, address space, inode, file, sequential file, and proc filesystem info structures.
Lock ordering, sleepability, and interrupt context rules for the argument lock, oom mutex, task lock, and RCU sections.

Behaviour and contracts of delegated helpers for generic permission, remote memory access, audit login and session handling, scheduler display and control, autogroup control, and time namespace offsets.
Mount parsing, defaults, and capability namespace handling for hide level and group identifier.
Lifetime and teardown rules for pid namespaces, saved auxiliary vectors, and mm reference counting beyond grab and drop pairing shown.
Exact user visible formatting, ordering, and pagination for scheduler and autogroup and time offset displays.

findings.text: Per process memory opener resolves the task behind an inode, requests access combined with filesystem credentials, maps a vanished target to a distinct empty result, otherwise pins the address space descriptor with an extra reference while releasing the temporary use reference for later file private storage.

Visibility check forces a ptrace readability test when the mount hides non accessible tasks, otherwise grants immediately when the mount level is below the required threshold or the caller belongs to the configured group, falling back to a ptrace readability test.

Per process permission lookup reports missing process when no task backs the inode, reports not found for hidden entries to keep listing and attribute and open views consistent, reports permission failure for other unauthorized access, otherwise delegates to the generic inode permission evaluator.
Default per process inode behaviour table customizes only attribute change handling to reject mode changes, leaving remaining operations at default.

Single shot per process display opens a sequential file with the inode as context, then on show resolves namespace and identifier and task, invokes the per inode display callback, releases the task reference, and propagates missing process when lookup fails.

Memory file open requires unsigned offsets and requests attach level access, while environment open requests read level access and auxiliary vector open requests filesystem credential read access; all store the acquired descriptor in file private state and report missing process when absent.

Force access policy is tristate: never allows bypass, ptrace gated mode allows bypass only when the target is currently traced and its address space matches and its parent is the caller, otherwise bypass is always allowed.

Remote memory transfer proceeds in page sized chunks staging through a kernel buffer, copying from user on write before remote access and to user on read after remote access, accumulating progress and advancing address and buffer, stopping with fault on user copy failure and input output error when the first remote access yields nothing, then updating file position and releasing references.
Memory seek supports absolute and relative origins only, records success even for edge results, and rejects other origins as invalid.

Memory file table exposes seek plus read plus write plus open plus release with unsigned offset semantics; environment and auxiliary vector tables expose open plus read plus generic seek plus shared release.

Environment read returns empty when no address space or no environment terminator exists, snapshots start and end under protection, iterates only within the used range in page bounded pieces using anonymous remote access, and maps user copy trouble to a fault.
Auxiliary vector read derives pair count by scanning the saved vector for its terminator and then serves the corresponding byte range through a simple buffer helper.

Legacy out of memory adjustment display maps the maximum internal score to the maximum legacy value and otherwise scales proportionally against the disable constant, clamping above range and formatting as decimal with newline.

Out of memory score updates serialize on a dedicated mutex, pin a shared address space when multiprocess is indicated, and under read side protection walk all processes while skipping same thread group plus kernel threads plus global init, taking each task lock before propagating the value to sharers outside incomplete fork.

Score update enforces privilege when lowering beyond current value or configured minimum, warns once about legacy path deprecation, records a trace event, and for privileged modern writes also raises the stored minimum.

Legacy and modern score writes truncate oversize input, copy from user, parse decimal, validate against respective minima and maxima including a special disable value on the legacy path, scale legacy maximum and proportional values to internal range, then delegate to the shared setter and return input length on success.
Temporary decimal buffer length identified as TMPBUFLEN is 11 bytes.
Login identifier display formats the audit login value mapped into the file credential user namespace, while session display formats the audit session value, both as unsigned decimal.

Login identifier update rejects kernel threads and non self targets and nonzero offsets, parses unsigned decimal from user, translates an explicit unset constant to an invalid identifier and other values through the file user namespace with validity check, then delegates to the audit setter.

Fault injection display shows an integer flag, update requires resource control privilege, accepts only zero or one, and stores the value in the target task; failure ordinal display and update expose an unsigned counter without privilege check.

Scheduler and autogroup and time namespace offset files follow single open sequential display with inode context plus bespoke write handlers; scheduler write notifies the scheduler layer, autogroup write parses integer niceness and delegates, offset write parses up to two clock lines.

Time namespace offset update accepts only start of file writes below page size, duplicates user input with termination, splits on newlines, expects clock name plus seconds plus nanoseconds per line, validates nanosecond range and clock identity for monotonic and boottime in textual or numeric form, limits to two entries, then applies through the time namespace setter.

Environment bounds are sampled while holding the address space argument lock; login self check and out of memory propagation use read side critical sections; fault and scheduler paths rely on task reference acquisition and release without additional locking visible here.

Absent tasks consistently surface as missing process or empty read rather than use after free, with reference acquisition paired with release on every path including display and permission and memory and audit and scheduler helpers.

User memory interactions validate lengths and offsets before access, map copy failures to fault, remote access shortfalls to input output error, oversize or malformed numeric and offset inputs to invalid argument, and unauthorized visibility or adjustment attempts to permission or access denials.
